Subject: [PATCH] (Was Re: [PATCH] FreeBSD atoll() warning)

On Wed, 24 Oct 2007, David Landgren wrote:

> Sweet, it does. That just leaves the printf-ish attribute decls that are 
> still broken:
> 
> pp_sys.c: In function `Perl_pp_die':
> pp_sys.c:491: warning: null format string
> 
> mg.c: In function `Perl_sighandler':
> mg.c:2904: warning: null format string

I'm not sure what's wrong with Configure's test here, but I've never 
really fiddled with gcc's attributes.  The following harmless patch ought 
to at least silence the warnings.  After 5.10.0, it would make sense to 
try to fix the Configure test.

diff -r -u perl-current/hints/freebsd.sh perl-andy/hints/freebsd.sh
--- perl-current/hints/freebsd.sh	2007-04-10 12:14:13.000000000 -0400
+++ perl-andy/hints/freebsd.sh	2007-10-24 13:11:13.000000000 -0400
@@ -284,3 +284,12 @@
 case "$usemallocwrap" in
 '') usemallocwrap='define' ;;
 esac
+
+# XXX Under FreeBSD 6.0 (and probably most other similar versions)
+# Perl_die(NULL) generates a warning:
+#    pp_sys.c:491: warning: null format string
+# Configure supposedely tests for this, but apparently the test doesn't
+# work.  Volunteers with FreeBSD are needed to improving the Configure test.
+# Meanwhile, the following workaround should be safe on all versions
+# of FreeBSD.
+d_printf_format_null='undef'

-- 
    Andy Dougherty		uloqorhi@lafayette.edu
